text.title: Activation Metrics Worked Example
text.summary: One complete weekly activation report for three closed signup weeks in April: `project_created` within 7 days at 0.223 against 5,335 signups, four channel rates with one low-sample flag, a partial metric for the open week, time-to-activation as median and p90, a D30 lift table from a March cohort, a five-step funnel with both drops, and three findings that cite metric and period, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the same report as it is usually written and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Activation was defined by the activation-framework spec as `project_created` within 7 days. The report covers signups from 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-26, pulled on 2026-05-04. A paid search campaign scaled up in April and onboarding checklist v2 shipped on 2026-04-13. The team's sample floor for a channel is 100 signups.

example.note: `period_end` is April 26 rather than May 3 because April 26 plus 7 days is May 3, inside the May 4 cutoff, while the week of April 27 is still open; that week appears only as `activation_rate_partial` (r-one-fixed-window-closed-cohorts-only). `activation_rate` is 1,192 / 5,335 where 5,335 is every signup in the period; the rate against email-verified users would be 0.306 and is not in the report (r-activation-rate-denominator-is-signups). The four channel denominators sum to 5,335 and the four numerators to 1,192; referral has 61 signups, below the floor of 100, so it is flagged `low_sample` and its finding says it is not compared (r-segment-by-acquisition-channel). Time-to-activation is a median of 1.4 hours with p75 and p90, which is why the report is in hours: half the users activate in the first session, and a mean of about two days would have hidden that (r-time-to-activation-uses-quantiles). The D30 table uses the March 2-8 cohort, whose last signup plus 30 days is April 7, well before the cutoff, with both sizes and the word correlation (r-d30-lift-table-with-sizes). Each funnel step carries `absolute_drop` = `entering` - `completing` and `relative_drop` to three decimals; "template picked" has no event and no numbers (r-funnel-steps-absolute-and-relative). Every metric is a ratio between 0 and 1 or a `pp` delta against `previous_period` (r-metric-naming-and-units). Each finding names the metric in its text and the period it is compared with; the checklist release is named with its date and `causal` stays false because it was not an A/B test (r-findings-cite-metric-and-period).

example.title: the same weeks as usually reported
example.note: What the validator prints: `activation_rate` has unit `percent`, which is not in the set, and its value 31 is not a ratio (r-metric-naming-and-units); `time_to_activation` has no `median` and no p75 or p90, only a mean (r-time-to-activation-uses-quantiles); the uninstrumented "template picked" step carries `entering` and `completing` (r-funnel-steps-absolute-and-relative); the finding is `causal: true` with no `ab_test_result` (r-findings-cite-metric-and-period). Once those are fixed the cross-field checks add: `period_end` May 3 plus 7 days is after the May 4 cutoff, so the open week is inside the rate (open-cohort-dip); `activation_rate.denominator` 4,780 is not `signups_total` 7,036, the rate was computed against users who reached a later step (narrowed-denominator); `activation_rate__referral` has 61 signups under the floor and no `low_sample` flag; the D30 cohort ends April 26, only 8 days before the cutoff, so its retention is a projection (d30-lift-without-sizes); "project created" has `absolute_drop` 1,600 where entering minus completing is 1,718; and the finding text never names `activation_rate` or the period. What the reviewer sees: a 31 percent rate that will not reconcile with finance, and a causal sentence about the checklist in a week when paid search changed the channel mix (channel-mix-read-as-product-change).
